slice: Yamaha WR250F/WR450F/YZ125X/YZ250X/YZ250FX/YZ450FX gap years, 2027 YZ125/YZ250/YZ450F, Honda CRF250RX 2020-2021 and CRF450RX 2020 - owner service manual specs, press and tests

records.statement: Yamaha's US owner's service manual for the 2021 WR250F identifies it as model WR250FM, model code BAK7; the manual is the US-market edition (Yamaha part BAK-2819U-11).
records.notes: Designation suffix letter is Yamaha's model-year code. Market editions for other regions carry other model codes.

records.statement: The 2021 WR250F engine is a liquid-cooled 250 cm³ DOHC four-stroke single, bore × stroke 77.0 × 53.6 mm (3.03 × 2.11 in), compression ratio 13.8 : 1, electric start, wet-sump lubrication.

Fuel injection with throttle body ID BAK1; fuel line pressure at idle 300–390 kPa (3.0–3.9 kgf/cm², 43.5–56.6 psi), idle speed 1900–2100 r/min; valve clearance (cold) intake 0.12–0.19 mm (0.0047–0.0075 in), exhaust 0.17–0.24 mm (0.0067–0.0094 in).
Engine control unit BAK2; TCI ignition with timing 8.0–12.0 /2000 r/min; fuel pump and electronic fuel injection.

records.topic: 2021 WR250F maps, Power Tuner and launch control
records.statement: On the US 2021 WR250F there is no handlebar map switch; fuel and ignition can be adjusted only with the optional handheld GYTR Power Tuner (33D-H59C0-V1-00) plugged into the coupler provided.
records.notes: US manual. Other markets (e.g. Europe/Australia) may ship with the app and switch where the US bike lists only the optional GYTR tuner.

records.statement: KYB coil-spring fork, 310 mm (12.2 in) travel, Yamaha Suspension Oil S1, 501.0 cm³ (16.94 US oz, 17.67 Imp.oz) per leg; standard clickers (counted out from fully in): rebound 8 of 20, compression 11 of 20.

KYB link shock, 317 mm (12.5 in) wheel travel; standard settings: spring preload 7.0 mm (0.28 in) turned in from free length, rebound 11 clicks out (of 30), high-speed compression 1 turns out, low-speed compression 8 clicks out.

Standard spring rates are 4.6 N/mm (fork) and None N/mm (shock); Yamaha lists optional fork springs from 4.1-5.1 N/mm. Rear sag is set to a sunken (rider-on) length of 90-100 mm before any other tuning.
records.notes: Spring tables in the Tuning chapter (front fork / rear shock absorber setting parts).

records.statement: Constant mesh 6-speed; primary reduction 3.353 (57/17); gear ratios 1st 2.385 (31/13), 2nd 1.813 (29/16), 3rd 1.444 (26/18), 4th 1.143 (24/21), 5th 0.957 (22/23), 6th 0.815 (22/27); secondary (final) reduction 3.923 (51/13), i.e. stock sprockets 13T front / 51T rear, chain final drive.

Wet multi-disc clutch: 2 pcs friction plate 1 (2.70–2.90 mm), 6 pcs friction plate 2 (2.72–2.88 mm), 7 pcs clutch plate (1.50–1.70 mm); clutch spring free length 44.00 mm (1.73 in); 520 sealed type chain, 114 links, slack 50.0–60.0 mm (1.97–2.36 in). Yamaha lists optional rear sprockets of 48, 50, 51, 52 teeth.
records.notes: Plate counts are listed in manual order (friction plate types first, then clutch/steel plates).

records.topic: 2021 WR250F overall gear ratios and speed per 1,000 rpm
records.statement: Worked out from Yamaha's ratios, overall reduction (engine to rear wheel) is 1st 31.37:1, 2nd 23.85:1, 3rd 18.99:1, 4th 15.03:1, 5th 12.59:1, 6th 10.72:1; on the stock 110/100-18 rear tire that is about 1st 4.07 km/h, 2nd 5.35 km/h, 3rd 6.72 km/h, 4th 8.49 km/h, 5th 10.14 km/h, 6th 11.91 km/h per 1,000 rpm.

source.name: BAK calculation from Yamaha 2021 WR250F OSM ratios

records.notes: overall = primary 3.353 x gear x secondary 3.923. Speed = rpm / overall x tire circumference; nominal rolling diameter 677 mm from 110/100-18 (rim x 25.4 + 2 x section x aspect), circumference 2.127 m, no tire squat or growth.

records.statement: Worked out from Yamaha's gearbox and stock sprockets: first gear gives about 4.07 km/h and top gear about 11.91 km/h per 1,000 rpm, so at 10,000 rpm first runs out near 41 km/h and top near 119 km/h (74 mph). The ratio between first and top gear is 2.93, a measure of how wide the box is.

records.topic: 2021 WR250F valve clearance and top end
records.statement: Valve clearance (cold) intake 0.12–0.19 mm (0.0047–0.0075 in), exhaust 0.17–0.24 mm (0.0067–0.0094 in); cylinder bore 77.000–77.010 mm (3.0315–3.0319 in) (wear limit 77.060 mm (3.0339 in)); piston-to-cylinder clearance 0.030–0.055 mm (0.0012–0.0022 in).

Yamaha's tuning chart for this model says: set rear sag (sunken length 90-100 mm) first; if the fork is stiff over its whole range back the compression out about 2 clicks, take 5-10 cc of oil out or fit a softer spring; if it is soft and bottoms, add about 2 clicks of compression or 5-10 cc of oil, or fit a stiffer spring; change oil in 5 cc steps for end-of-stroke feel. After a softer spring go 1-2 clicks out on rebound, after a stiffer one 1-2 clicks in.

records.statement: Yamaha's 2020 service manual (shared with the YZ125) lists the YZ125X as model YZ125XL for the USA, Canada and Australia, model code B1B5 (USA, Canada) and B1B6 (Australia); 2020 was its first year.

The 2020 YZ125X uses the YZ125's 125 cc 54.0 x 54.5 mm reed-valve two-stroke but with a bigger combustion chamber: 10.0-10.2 cc against 8.30-8.50 cc on the YZ125, lowering compression to 7.4-8.8:1 (YZ125 8.6-10.7:1). Reeds 0.470 mm thick, stopper height 8.2-8.6 mm.

Carbureted with a Mikuni TMX38SS. The manual's US/Canada jetting: I.D. 1C37 51, main jet #430, needle 6BFY43-74 clip 3, cutaway 4, pilot jet #40, pilot air screw 2-1/4 turns out, valve seat 3.8 mm, starter jet #80, fuel level 9.5-10.5 mm. CDI ignition with a digital advancer, timing 0.50 mm BTDC; no map switch.
records.notes: The 2020 manual's jetting table is not split by model; the YZ125X-only 2021 manual (B1B-2819U-10) lists the identical #430/6BFY43-74-3/#40/2-1/4 setting, so it applies to the X.

records.statement: Engine controls on the 2020 YZ125X are a CDI with digital advancer and the mechanical YPVS power valve; Yamaha lists no handlebar map switch or selectable ignition map.

KYB 48 mm inner-tube coil fork, 300 mm travel, standard spring 4.10 N/mm, 425 cc of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 per leg on the YZ125X (510 cc on the YZ125), damper oil level 145-148 mm; standard rebound 11 clicks out, compression 15 clicks out (of 20); fork tubes 5 mm above the top clamp.

KYB shock, 315 mm wheel travel (131.5 mm shaft), standard spring 46 N/mm (red, 260 mm free length) set to a 254 mm fitting length on the X (252 mm YZ125), preload range 1.5-18 mm; standard rebound 12-15 clicks out, low-speed compression 12-15 clicks out, high-speed compression 1-5/8 +/- 1/6 turns out; 1,000 kPa nitrogen.
Yamaha's manual gives the X's standard fork rebound as 11 clicks out; one magazine test listed 9 as stock and also ran 4.1 N/mm fork and 46 N/mm shock springs with 105 mm race sag.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2020 Yamaha YZ125X cross-country

records.notes: Kept side by side: the OSM figure is the authoritative standard.

records.statement: Six-speed close-ratio box: primary 3.368 (64/19), gears 2.385, 1.933, 1.588, 1.353, 1.200, 1.095; final drive 50/13 (3.846) on the X versus 48/13 on the YZ125. Optional rear sprockets 47-52 teeth; drive chain D.I.D 520MXV5 O-ring, 114 links.
Wet multi-plate clutch with 8 friction plates (2.90-3.10 mm, limit 2.80) and 7 steel plates, five springs of 40.10 mm free length (limit 38.10); inner-push cam release; kick-and-mesh kickstarter.

records.topic: YZ125X engine differences from the YZ125 (2020-2022)
records.statement: Versus the YZ125 the first-generation X lowers compression partly by raising the spark plug 3 mm, uses stiffer power-valve springs and a reshaped valve so the YPVS starts opening at 8,000 rpm (YZ 7,500) and is fully open at 10,250 rpm (YZ 9,500), lowers the exhaust port 0.5 mm, and advances ignition about 5 degrees low to mid while retarding it slightly mid to top.

records.notes: Magazine report of the 2020 changes; Yamaha manuals for 2021 and 2022 list the same compression, jetting and gearing, so the same engine spec is assumed.

records.statement: The first-generation YZ125X has a milder, more tractable powerband than the YZ125, deliberately giving up some peak for control in tight, slow going.

records.statement: Testers' main complaints: the 8 L (2.1 gal) tank gives roughly 40 minutes of hard riding, there is no skid plate or hand guards (cases, water pump and ignition exposed), the motocross-ratio gearbox with taller final drive leaves limited gear options, and the stock AT81 tires work poorly on motocross tracks.

records.statement: Yamaha introduced the 2023 YZ125X with a completely redesigned 125 two-stroke (more power and usability than the 2022), revised YPVS timing, a model-specific 3D-map digital CDI, a new Keihin PWK38S carburetor with power jet, a revised close-ratio six-speed with wider gear teeth, revised suspension damping, new brakes, new YZ styling and new ergonomics.
Yamaha describes the 2023 YZ125X engine as an increase in power and usability over the 2022 model, with broad, usable delivery aimed at cross-country and enduro racing.
The 2023 YZ125X uses its own digital CDI with 3D-map ignition timing (different from the YZ125 motocrosser) plus revised YPVS timing for low-mid tractability.
Yamaha describes the 2027 YZ125X engine as giving strong acceleration and exciting mid-to-high rpm power with good usability.

For 2027 Yamaha lists a Keihin PWK38S carburetor with power jet and throttle position sensor, a 3D-map CDI and a model-specific digital CDI unit compared with the YZ125, plus optimized YPVS settings; there are no selectable maps.
Yamaha specifies a 48 mm Speed Sensitive System KYB fork and a fully adjustable KYB shock with Kashima-coated internals, both with a cross-country-focused setup.

Testers found the second-generation X surprisingly torquey for a 125: it can lug a taller gear without an immediate downshift yet still likes to rev, and it has less engine braking than the motocross bike, which helps carry momentum.
records.notes: Test of the 2024; Yamaha manuals list identical engine/carb/gearbox specs 2023-2027.

records.statement: Common complaints on the 2023-on X: no electric start and the motocross-size 7.0 L (1.8 gal) tank, which limits range on long loops; heavier or faster riders may want the cross-country valving stiffened for high-speed terrain.
records.notes: Tank size from Yamaha manuals 2023-2027.

records.statement: The KYB fork and shock run softer settings than the YZ125 and absorb repeated rock, root and braking-bump hits better, with slower rebound that uses all the travel.
Yamaha's 2020 service manual (shared with the YZ250) lists the YZ250X as model YZ250XL for the USA, Canada and Australia, model code BF1H (USA, Canada) and BF1K (Australia).

249 cc 66.4 x 72.0 mm reed-valve two-stroke; the X's combustion chamber is 23.45-23.75 cc against 21.35-21.65 cc on the YZ250, giving 7.9-9.4:1 compression (YZ250 8.9-10.6:1). Reeds 0.420 mm, stopper height 10.3-10.7 mm; Keihin PWK38S carburetor.

Carbureted Keihin PWK38S, US/Canada jetting: I.D. 1P87 50, main #178, main air jet #200, needle N3EW clip 2, needle jet 2.9, cutaway #7, pilot #50, air screw 1-1/4 turns, valve seat 3.8 mm, starter #85, power jet #50, float arm height 6.5 mm. CDI ignition, YPVS governor, no map switch.
records.notes: Table is not split by model; the 2021 and 2022 YZ250X manuals list the same jetting.

records.statement: KYB 48 mm coil fork, 300 mm travel, standard spring 4.30 N/mm (same as YZ250), 515 cc S1 oil per leg, damper oil level 145-148 mm; standard rebound 10 clicks out, compression 13 out (of 20).

KYB shock, 315 mm travel, standard spring 48 N/mm (black, 260 mm free length) at a 248 mm fitting length, preload range 1.5-18 mm; standard rebound 10-13 clicks out, low-speed compression 11-14 out, high-speed 1-5/8 +/- 1/6 turns out.

Five-speed: primary 3.000 (63/21); X ratios 1.929, 1.533, 1.313, 1.050, 0.840 (YZ250: 3rd 1.278, 4th 1.091, 5th 0.952); final 50/14 (3.571); optional sprockets 13-14 front and 47-52 rear; D.I.D 520VM2 chain, 114 links.
8 friction plates (2.90-3.10 mm), 7 steel plates and six clutch springs of 44.00 mm free length on the X (50.00 mm on the YZ250) for a lighter pull; ratchet kickstarter.

records.statement: The X is milder and more tractable than the YZ250, with a perky low-to-mid pull suited to rocky, tight terrain that lets riders go faster with less hesitation, but it is not a motocross start-line powerband.

records.statement: Yamaha specifies a cross-country-tuned 48 mm Speed Sensitive KYB fork with 11.8 in travel and a fully adjustable KYB shock with 12.4 in travel.

records.statement: For 2022 the WR250F got new cam profiles and intake port for a broader spread with better high-rpm power, a new shift cam for smoother shifting, and a new aluminum bilateral beam frame derived from the YZ250F; US MSRP rose $200 to $8,799.

records.notes: Magazine summary of Yamaha information.

records.statement: Testers found the 2022 engine stronger across the range, especially mid to top where it revs more freely, so gears can be held longer.
records.notes: European test of the 2022; US manuals show 2023-2024 engine specs unchanged.

records.statement: Stalling and awkward hot restarts remain a WR250F trait though better than earlier models; it stalls more readily than a two-stroke in technical going, and a softer map reduces stalling.
With only about 0.95 L of engine oil (dry fill), testers advise frequent oil changes on the WR250F.
records.notes: Yamaha manuals list 0.95 L disassembled capacity.

records.statement: European-market 2022 WR250Fs were tested with the Power Tuner smartphone app and a handlebar switch between full and softer maps; the US 2022-2024 manuals list neither, only the optional handheld GYTR Power Tuner.
The 2027 WR250F returns unchanged with a US MSRP of $9,199.

source.name: Dirt Rider - 2022 Yamaha enduro motorcycles first look

records.topic: WR450F traction control via Power Tuner
records.statement: Yamaha's WR450F has a three-level traction control (HIGH, LOW, OFF) enabled through the Power Tuner app, which reads wheel slip into the ECU; ECU settings are tailored for trail and enduro.
records.notes: 2025 features page; the 2026 US manual lists identical specs and the same app/CCU and mode switch.

records.statement: Yamaha says the WR450F's 450 cc DOHC engine is light and compact with strong pulling power, and its high rev limit helps over-rev for a broad power character.
Yamaha lists a compact disc-spring clutch whose primary gear and basket are one steel unit, and a wide-ratio five-speed gearbox for off-road use.
Fully adjustable KYB coil fork with speed-sensitive damping and a new hand-operated compression clicker for tool-free changes.
Aluminum bilateral beam frame of more than ten welded components with WR450F-specific engine mounts.

Testers found the 2025 WR450F fast and willing to rev, with low first gear for crawling and enough torque in second and third to pull out of corners with little clutch; the mellow handlebar map tames it for slippery going.

source.name: Australasian Dirt Bike - Enduro test: 2025 Yamaha WR450F

records.notes: Australian test of a 2025; the 2026 US manual lists identical specs.

records.statement: The flameout problem of older WRs is mostly gone, though bogging it in too high a gear can still make it sputter; the suspension can feel a little firm at slow pace and the 955 mm seat is tall.

source.name: Australasian Dirt Bike - Enduro test: 2025 Yamaha WR450F

records.statement: Start on the mellow map (blue light) in slick conditions and switch to full power once the ground dries; back off compression damping for a softer ride at slow pace.

source.name: Australasian Dirt Bike - Enduro test: 2025 Yamaha WR450F

records.statement: For 2027 the WR450F takes the latest YZ450F engine tuned for low and midrange, with a revised intake port, new cam timing and a heavier AC magneto rotor to smooth low-rpm delivery and resist stalling, plus a new air filter assembly, lighter throttle and quieter resonator.

records.notes: Magazine summary of Yamaha information.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2027 Yamaha WR450F first look

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2027 Yamaha WR450F first look

records.notes: Measured on a 2022; the 2022 and 2023 US manuals list identical specifications.

records.statement: Testers found exceptional low-end torque for a 250F that lets it lug and chug, a strong mid-range and a top end competitive with the highest-revving 250s; gears 3-6 pull better than before so first and second are rarely needed.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - First impression: 2022 Yamaha YZ250FX

source.name: Yamaha Motor New Zealand - 2027 YZ450FX spec sheet

The 2027 YZ125 and YZ250 carry on with updated Icon Blue colours and graphics only, plus Monster Energy Edition versions; no mechanical changes were announced.
The 2027 YZ450F is also offered as a Monster Energy Edition in team livery; its frame, suspension, clutch and dry-sump layout serve as the base for the all-new 2027 YZ250F.

records.topic: 2020 CRF250 engine and chassis update (shared by RX)
records.statement: Honda's 2020 update for the CRF250R/RX claimed 4% more power at 12,000 rpm (peak 1,000 rpm lower), 8% more peak torque at 10,000 rpm and 10% more at 8,000 rpm, rev limit slightly lower at 14,300 rpm, via new cams, ports and piston, bigger radiator, new downpipe and a 10% larger filter; frame and swingarm tweaks from the 2019 CRF450R saved 350 g; more low-speed damping; and gear-position-based ignition maps.
records.notes: Honda's claims as reported in a press summary; 2021 is a carry-over.

records.statement: 249.43 cc liquid-cooled four-stroke single inclined 9 deg from vertical, bore x stroke 79.000 x 50.887 mm, compression 13.9:1, throttle body GQA7A, idle 2,000 +/- 100 rpm; valve clearance (cold) intake 0.09 +/- 0.03 mm, exhaust 0.19 +/- 0.03 mm.

records.topic: CRF250RX engine modes and launch control (2020-2021)
records.statement: Three PGM-FI engine modes selected by the handlebar button: mode 1 standard, mode 2 smooth (softer response), mode 3 aggressive (sharper response); HRC launch control with three levels (factory level 2) temporarily lowers the rev limit for the start. The 2020 250RX manual lists no torque (traction) control.

Showa coil fork, 305 mm stroke and 268 mm wheel travel; RX standard spring 4.6 N/mm (options 4.4 and 4.8), standard oil 356 cc (range about 306-391 cc), damper oil 243 cc; standard compression 12 clicks and rebound 15 clicks out from fully in (CRF250R 9 and 11).

Honda's manual says the RX fork's minimum oil with the standard spring is 306 cc; to cure big-bump harshness turn compression out one click and lower oil in 5 cc steps without going below the minimum; optional softer and stiffer fork and shock springs are listed for rider weight.

records.topic: 2020 CRF450RX modes, HSTC and launch control
records.statement: Three PGM-FI modes (1 standard, 2 smooth, 3 aggressive); Torque Control (HSTC) with modes 1, 2 and 3 plus off - mode 1 allows the most rear-wheel slip and mode 3 the least, factory mode 2, inactive on deceleration; HRC launch control with three levels (factory level 2) lowers the rev limit and works with Torque Control off the start, cancelling in third gear.

Showa coil fork, 305 mm stroke, 268 mm travel; RX standard spring 4.8 N/mm (options 4.6 and 5.0), 363 cc standard oil (minimum 309 cc with standard spring), damper oil 243 cc; standard compression 8 clicks, rebound 15 clicks out from fully in. Honda says the stock springs suit riders of about 77-91 kg without gear.

Pro-Link shock, 312 mm travel on the RX; standard spring 52 N/mm (options 50 and 54; the R uses 56) at 233.5 mm preload length (227-239 mm); high-speed compression 3-1/6 turns out (+/- 1/4), low-speed 10 clicks, rebound 8-11 clicks; 105 mm race sag.
The RX's Showa fork and shock are a little softer than the motocross bike's but still take a massive hit to bottom, and bottoming is well controlled.
